title: emergencyTransfer sweeps phUSD/rewardToken without zeroing accounting, permanently bricking pauseWithdraw and turning the documented 'emergency exit' into a principal-loss trap
rootCause: `emergencyTransfer` moves `phUSD.balanceOf(this)` and `rewardToken.balanceOf(this)` to an arbitrary owner-chosen recipient and `_pause()`s the contract, but does not zero or reconcile `totalStaked`, `userInfo[*]`, `rewardBalance`, or per-user debts. After invocation: (a) `withdraw` is gated by `whenNotPaused` and would in any case revert at the final `phUSD.safeTransfer` (no balance); (b) `pauseWithdraw` is reachable while paused but ALSO reverts at `phUSD.safeTransfer` because the contract holds zero phUSD; (c) the documented 'emergency exit mechanism' is therefore silently inoperable. No timelock, no multisig, no on-chain refund path.
impactSummary: Every staked principal can be removed by a single owner transaction. Stakers retain on-chain entitlements (userInfo[u].amount > 0) against a vault with zero balance and no on-chain redemption mechanism. The 'pauseWithdraw' fallback users are told to rely on is silently broken by the same call.
preservedDetails: CODE-003 carries the strongest implementation-level framing (accounting drift / on-chain DoS). ECON-005 carries the economic/principal-loss framing and the 'documented emergency exit mechanism is silently broken' angle. PATTERN-004 carries the structural CENTRALIZATION-ADMIN pattern match (single-tx rug). ADERYN-005 is the raw SAST centralization signal on line 214 (subsumed).
remediation: Either (a) restrict the sweep to the EXCESS balance only (`balanceOf - totalStaked` for phUSD; `balanceOf - rewardBalance` for rewardToken), preserving user-exit invariant; (b) zero `totalStaked`/`rewardBalance` and flag a global shutdown so pauseWithdraw can be gated to revert with a meaningful error; (c) add a `refillForExit` path callable by anyone post-emergency; (d) add a long timelock specifically on `emergencyTransfer` so users have time to pauseWithdraw beforehand.

consolidationRationale.CODE-003: Implementation-level: accounting drift / DoS of pauseWithdraw.
consolidationRationale.ECON-005: Economic-level: principal loss + intent-mismatch with the 'emergency exit' guarantee.

dedupNotes: All four sources point to the same single function on the same line with the same remediation. Strongest framing is CODE-003 (concrete on-chain DoS) augmented with ECON-005 (economic impact narrative). PATTERN-004 carves out the 'centralization that escalates because it enables a one-tx rug', avoiding the usual C4 'centralization-Low' demotion.
